subject: physics_2
question_text: Two wires of equal length, made of copper and manganin, have the same resistance. Which wire is thicker?

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: A = ρl/R, so with l and R equal, A ∝ ρ; resistivity of manganin (≈ 44 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m) is much larger than copper's (≈ 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m), so the manganin wire needs the larger cross-section — manganin is thicker, as the book concludes.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: A ∝ ρ from R = ρl/A
lines: The lengths are equal and the resistances
steps.margin_note: First mark. Fix l and R, and the area is forced to follow the resistivity.
steps.why: With l and R held equal, the only free quantities left in R = ρl/A are ρ and A, and they must rise together for R to stay the same.
common_mistakes: Concluding A ∝ 1/ρ. Solve for A: it sits with ρ on the same side, so more resistivity needs MORE area.
Comparing the resistances instead of the areas — the resistances are given equal.

recall.must_convey: That from R equals rho l by A, with equal l and R, the area is proportional to the resistivity.
accept: area follows resistivity when l and R are same
from R equals rho l by A

steps.memory_tip: Same R, same l: whatever has more ρ must take more A.

steps.label: Manganin is thicker
lines: The resistivity of manganin is much larger
So the manganin wire needs the larger
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the fact (manganin's ρ is larger) and then the conclusion.
steps.why: Manganin is an alloy, and alloys have larger resistivity than their pure metals. To offer the same resistance over the same length despite that, manganin must be spread over a larger area.
common_mistakes: Answering copper because it conducts better — better conduction means copper can be THINNER, not thicker.

recall.must_convey: That manganin has the larger resistivity, so the manganin wire is the thicker one.
accept: manganin has more resistivity than copper

steps.memory_tip: The worse conductor must be fatter to keep up — manganin is thicker.

insider_note: The trap is answering copper by instinct. Writing A ∝ ρ first makes the right answer fall out on its own.
